sources.entry: 3. DevSecOps What Why And How (BlackHat USA-19)

summary.title: DevSecOps: What, Why and How? (BlackHat USA 2019)
summary.one_liner: Learn what DevSecOps is, why it matters, and where security checks (pre-commit hooks, SAST, SCA, DAST, IaC, compliance as code) fit into a DevOps pipeline.
keywords: how to add security to devops pipeline
takeaways: DevSecOps means integrating security into DevOps through automation and cultural change, aiming for secure by default.
Shifting left, i.e. finding bugs earlier in the pipeline, is far cheaper than fixing them in production.
Security checks can be placed at each pipeline stage: pre-commit hooks and IDE plugins, SAST and SCA before build, DAST after build, and IaC and compliance checks at staging and production.
Pre-commit hooks, IDE plugins and secrets management help stop leaked credentials, but should be treated as defense in depth rather than relied on alone.
A central vulnerability management dashboard is needed to normalize tool reports and feed findings into bug trackers.
summary.summary: This BlackHat USA 2019 slide deck by Anant Shrivastava introduces DevSecOps and argues that traditional security cannot keep up with rapid DevOps delivery. It walks through a DevOps pipeline and shows where to inject security controls: pre-commit hooks, IDE plugins, secrets management, software composition analysis, SAST before build, DAST after build, security in infrastructure as code, compliance as code, and alerting. It ends with vulnerability management, where a central dashboard consolidates tool output and links to bug tracking. The deck is a high-level overview with a stated disclaimer that it does not endorse specific tools, and it names few concrete tools or implementation details.
